text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following its lightning raid on the sharemarket on Wednesday, Canadian mining giant Placer Dome Inc yesterday announced a A$400 million cash bid for Highlands Gold and at the same time launched a A$310 million scrip offer for the outstanding shares in its Australian offshoot, Placer Pacific Ltd. Page 1.

Last Friday's announcement that Janet Holmes a Court's John Holland construction group had just been sacked as building contractor on a A$250 million project at Mobil's Altona oil refinery calls into question the bankability of Janet Holmes a Court and the future of the ability of her company to make big tenders. Page 1.

Lend Lease chairman Stuart Hornery, Qantas managing director James Strong and BHP managing director John Prescott have all distanced themselves from independent MP Pauline Hanson's views and spoken of their enthusiasm for Asia and connections with the region in cable-TV specials which will go to air this week on CNBC. Page 4.

As Trans-Tasman brewer and soft drinks group Lion Nathan attempts to claw back market share from its arch rival Foster's Brewing Group and struggles to make profits from its A$200 million Australasian Pepsi joint venture, it has received news of the exit of another senior executive, chief operating officer Kevin Roberts. Page 29.

Sparked by a growing perception that members of the controlling Ainsworth family may start to sell down their shareholding when a voluntary escrow period ends in mid-January and by the appointment of John Dougall as executive chairman, investors wiped anoher A$42 million off the market value of poker machine manufacturer Aristocrat Leisure Ltd yesterday. Page 29.

Elders Australia Ltd yesterday bought 2.7 million Primac Holdings Ltd shares at A$3.20 each, giving it a stake rivalling the near 17 percent stake held by the Victorian co-operative Pivot Ltd and delivering a blow to IAMA Ltd's takeover aspirations for Primac. Page 31.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia's banks can look forward to a major shake-up, with the Wallis inquiry into the financial system encouraging non-banks and foreign competition to battle for traditional banking business. The interim report released yesterday has also indicated a review of the criteria for assessing bank takeovers. Page 23.

Canadian gold group Placer Dome Inc has launched a A$450 million takeover bid for PNG-based Highlands Gold Ltd to get Highlands' share of the 1.1 million ounce a year Porgera gold mine. Placer Dome also launched a second takeover bid to buy out minoriy shareholders in its 75.4 per cent-owned local subsidiary Placer Pacific Ltd. Page 23.

Pay TV operator Australis Media has appointed Optus Vision executive Sean O'Halloran as its new chief executive officer. The appointment follows the launch of a joint venture with Optus which involves sharing infrastructure and subscription management beteen the two operators. Page 23.

Helix Resources NL has secured nearly A$14 million through a share placement offer. An additional 4.2 million shares were issued for the group, which has become the driving force behind a South Australian gold rush. The speed with which the shares were snapped up reflects the market's confidence in the gold production potential of South Australia's Gawler Craton region. Page 25.

Qantas Airways managing director James Strong believes proposals to fine aircraft breaching tough new noise limits at London airports could cost the Australian carrier tens of thousands of dollars. He said Asia-Pacific airlines were most likely to breach the limits as carriers would operate fully laden 747 aircraft on long-haul routes from London. Page 25.

Financial inquiry chairman Stan Wallis believes that if the federal government wants free banking for low income earners, it should foot the bill. Wallis believes that it is inherently the government's responsibility to provide free banking services, not the pivate sector. Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Vancouver-based Placer Dome Inc has launched two takeover bids valued at A$742 million to secure a foothold in the Pacific region. The Canadian group took out 33 percent of PNG-based gold producer Highlands Gold. The second offer was a clean-up offer for Placer Pacific in which it already has a 75 percent interest. Page 27.

The Adelaide Steamship Co has appointed two advisers to assist with a A$150-million capital raising bid involving its marine towage business. Adsteam plans to either publicly float Adsteam Marine or keep the business and have a A$150-million rights issue to refinance the parent. Page 27.

With Sausage Software shareholders seeing their stock fall 60 percent in the six weeks since the public float of the Australian Internet company, Sausage Software executives face an angry annual meeting today as they try to explain the company's dismal prformance. Responding to an Australian Stock Exchange query over the sharp fall in Sausage's share price, company secretary Jim Paulshyn said he was unaware of any information that would unduly affect the share price. Page 27.

New Reserve Bank Governor Ian McFarlane has criticised union wage claims in the metals industry for a 15 percent rise over the next two years, saying the metal industry faces intense international pressure and could not pass on wage rises into product prces. McFarlane also attacked executive pay rises, claiming they set a bad example. Page 27.

Pay TV group Australis Media has appointed former Seven Network executive Sean O'Halloran as its chief executive officer, replacing Neil Gamble, who left to take up the top management job at the Sydney Harbour Casino. The appointment of O'Halloran is anoher example of how close Australis is to rival Optus Vision following the announcement in August that it was entering a satellite facility joint venture agreement with Optus as part of an overall A$380 million rescue package. Page 29.

Ten Group shareholders Robert Whyte and Jack Cowin have placed their combined 10 percent interest in the television group up for sale, placing their 9.12 million shares on the market at A$15.00 each, valuing the network at a staggering A$1.38 billion. Page 29.
THE AGE

Canadian mining giant Placer Dome Inc has launched twin takeover bids for Highlands Gold and Placer Pacific, sparked by the poor share price performance of both companies. Placer plans to spend A$313 million in scrip absorbing the 24.6 percent of Placer Pacific it does not already own, and A$423 million for Highlands Gold. Page C1.

After losing two chief executives of its Australian operations in a matter of months and a host of other senior managers, New Zealand-based brewer Lion Nathan has been rocked by the news of the departure of long-serving chief operating officer Kevin Roberts. Roberts has worked as the right-hand man of Lion's major shareholder and chief executive, Douglas Myers, for the past eight years. Page C1.

Speaking at the release of the Financial System Inquiry committee's interim discussion paper yesterday, inquiry chairman Stan Wallis gave his strongest hint yet that mergers between the big four banks and two big life insurers would be allowed, after he said the majority of submissions to the inquiry argued that it was hard to find a rationale for the restrictions. Page C1.

Sausage Software founder Steve Outtrim faces a hostile annual meeting today following the company's dismal sharemarket performance since listing six weeks ago. Australia's first publicly floated Internet company, Sausage has come under scrutiny by the Australian Stock Exchange but has so far been unable to explain the dip in share price. Page C1.

The wool industry taskforce report, presented to the acting Victorian Premier and Agriculture and Resources Minister Pat McNamara yesterday revealed there are still too many small and unproductive sheep farms blocking the emergence of a competitive and viable Australian industry. The report recommended the rules be changed to give aid to better-off farmers. Page C3.

With Ballarat Goldfields NL's share price rising from 5.8 cents a share at the start of the month to 8.5 cents yesterday, there is an expectation that shareholders at today's meeting in Ballarat will receive good news on how management plans to restart the Ballarat East gold project. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
